root_cause.text: `rxgk_extract_token()` in the rxrpc/RXGK token parsing path failed to propagate `-ENOMEM` from `rxgk_decrypt_skb()` and instead continued execution, leading to an erroneous connection abort/error handling path on an out-of-memory failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `return ret;` immediately after `if (ret != -ENOMEM)` in `net/rxrpc/rxgk_app.c`, and the commit message says “in the event that `rxgk_decrypt_skb()` returns `-ENOMEM`, it should just return that rather than continuing on (for anything else, it generates an abort).”

intent_record.intent_summary: Return immediately on -ENOMEM to avoid continuing into ticket decoding after allocation failure.
intent_record.what: In the error-handling block after a call that can return -ENOMEM, a new `return ret;` statement was inserted immediately after the existing `if (ret != -ENOMEM) return rxrpc_abort_conn(...)` check.
intent_record.how: This changes control flow so that when the earlier operation fails with `-ENOMEM`, the function now returns that error code directly instead of falling through to the subsequent ticket-decoding logic. It prevents later code from running after an out-of-memory failure.

candidates.rationale: This condition shows the pre-fix logic that only returned early for errors other than -ENOMEM. When rxgk_decrypt_skb() failed with -ENOMEM, execution continued into ticket decoding instead of stopping, which is the root cause.
This is the abort path that was incorrectly taken for non-ENOMEM errors while -ENOMEM was allowed to fall through. The vulnerability stems from not returning here on allocation failure.
This statement represents the erroneous continuation after a decrypt allocation failure. Continuing into ticket decoding after -ENOMEM is the directly vulnerable behavior.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition allowed execution to continue when rxgk_decrypt_skb() returned -ENOMEM, rather than returning immediately. That fall-through is the root cause of the invalid continuation into ticket decoding after an allocation failure.

The function also has a separate `cant_get_token:` path that explicitly treats `-ENOMEM` as a temporary error via `goto temporary_error; return ret;`, which is the correct handling. Therefore the buggy behavior described in the root cause is absent here, and the code already contains the fix.
